lessons.title: Protocols and shared resources
lessons.prepare: Open the networks chapter and its learning resources. Use paper or a local editor as appropriate, with fictional data and disposable practice copies. The suggested 55-minute lesson is flexible.

slides.title: Protocols and shared resources
body: Unit 1 · Week 11 · Lesson 1
Explain why networked devices need shared rules.
slides.notes: Explain the goal and the expected independent outcome. Explain why networked devices need shared rules. This is ungraded textbook learning. Suggested times can be adjusted to the class. Teaching reference: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#networks. Technical/course references: https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc1122 https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc1918 https://senior-secondary.scsa.wa.edu.au/__data/assets/pdf_file/0003/1090875/Year-11_12_Computer-Science_ATAR_Additional-syllabus-support-booklet-.PDF

slides.title: Retrieval and explanation
body: Which school resources do devices share?
What could go wrong if message formats differ?
slides.notes: Examples include files, printers and a web service. Shared formats and responses let devices interpret a request. A cable alone does not specify the message meaning. Allow silent thinking before discussion. Ask a learner to justify an answer before revealing the explanation. Teaching reference: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#networks. Technical/course references: https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc1122 https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc1918 https://senior-secondary.scsa.wa.edu.au/__data/assets/pdf_file/0003/1090875/Year-11_12_Computer-Science_ATAR_Additional-syllabus-support-booklet-.PDF

slides.title: A network request
slides.notes: Distinguish a service from its communication rules and physical connection. Use the fictional library scenario. Teaching reference: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#networks. Technical/course references: https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc1122 https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc1918 https://senior-secondary.scsa.wa.edu.au/__data/assets/pdf_file/0003/1090875/Year-11_12_Computer-Science_ATAR_Additional-syllabus-support-booklet-.PDF

slides.title: A useful request
body: One device sends a request for a library page.
The service interprets it and returns a response.
Name a rule both ends need to agree on.
slides.notes: Accept message format, request meaning or response interpretation. HTTP is an application protocol. More layers handle transport and local delivery. Pause for predictions before discussing the expected result. Teaching reference: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#networks. Technical/course references: https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc1122 https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc1918 https://senior-secondary.scsa.wa.edu.au/__data/assets/pdf_file/0003/1090875/Year-11_12_Computer-Science_ATAR_Additional-syllabus-support-booklet-.PDF

slides.title: Protocol sorting
body: Match web requests, email transfer and name lookup.
Use HTTP, SMTP and DNS.
Explain the job of each choice.
slides.notes: HTTP handles web messages, SMTP transfers email, DNS provides name-related lookup information. HTTPS protects HTTP using TLS. Swap explaining and checking roles so both learners articulate the reasoning. Teaching reference: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#networks. Technical/course references: https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc1122 https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc1918 https://senior-secondary.scsa.wa.edu.au/__data/assets/pdf_file/0003/1090875/Year-11_12_Computer-Science_ATAR_Additional-syllabus-support-booklet-.PDF

slides.title: Independent practice
body: Choose a shared resource.
Describe its client, request and response.
Explain why a connection and agreed rules matter.
slides.notes: Pairs draft first, then each learner explains a changed resource independently. Accept a printer example if its service and rules are distinguished clearly. Offer the relevant worked example if needed, then use a changed case to check independent understanding. Teaching reference: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#networks. Technical/course references: https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc1122 https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc1918 https://senior-secondary.scsa.wa.edu.au/__data/assets/pdf_file/0003/1090875/Year-11_12_Computer-Science_ATAR_Additional-syllabus-support-booklet-.PDF

slides.title: A choice to explain
body: Two devices share a cable connection.
A: That alone defines every service message.
B: They still need shared communication rules.
slides.notes: B. Connectivity and agreement about message meaning are different requirements. Give thinking time and collect reasons, without recording scores. Teaching reference: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#networks. Technical/course references: https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc1122 https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc1918 https://senior-secondary.scsa.wa.edu.au/__data/assets/pdf_file/0003/1090875/Year-11_12_Computer-Science_ATAR_Additional-syllabus-support-booklet-.PDF

slides.title: Exit explanation
body: Define protocol in your own words.
Apply the definition to a new resource.
slides.notes: A useful answer names agreed rules and links them to interpreting an actual request or response. Use the response to select the next explanation or practice activity. Teaching reference: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#networks. Technical/course references: https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc1122 https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc1918 https://senior-secondary.scsa.wa.edu.au/__data/assets/pdf_file/0003/1090875/Year-11_12_Computer-Science_ATAR_Additional-syllabus-support-booklet-.PDF

lessons.title: The four TCP/IP layers
lessons.prepare: Open the networks chapter and its learning resources. Use paper or a local editor as appropriate, with fictional data and disposable practice copies. The suggested 55-minute lesson is flexible.

slides.title: The four TCP/IP layers
body: Unit 1 · Week 11 · Lesson 2
Match each layer to a communication responsibility.
slides.notes: Explain the goal and the expected independent outcome. Match each layer to a communication responsibility. This is ungraded textbook learning. Suggested times can be adjusted to the class. Teaching reference: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#networks. Technical/course references: https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc1122 https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc1918 https://senior-secondary.scsa.wa.edu.au/__data/assets/pdf_file/0003/1090875/Year-11_12_Computer-Science_ATAR_Additional-syllabus-support-booklet-.PDF

slides.title: Retrieval and explanation
body: What job does HTTP perform?
Which other jobs must carry its messages?
slides.notes: HTTP describes application messages. Transport, IP routing and a local link have separate responsibilities. Allow silent thinking before discussion. Ask a learner to justify an answer before revealing the explanation. Teaching reference: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#networks. Technical/course references: https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc1122 https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc1918 https://senior-secondary.scsa.wa.edu.au/__data/assets/pdf_file/0003/1090875/Year-11_12_Computer-Science_ATAR_Additional-syllabus-support-booklet-.PDF

slides.title: Four responsibilities
slides.notes: The course may call the bottom layer Network. It is not the OSI Network layer. Explain the model label before comparing answers. Teaching reference: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#networks. Technical/course references: https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc1122 https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc1918 https://senior-secondary.scsa.wa.edu.au/__data/assets/pdf_file/0003/1090875/Year-11_12_Computer-Science_ATAR_Additional-syllabus-support-booklet-.PDF

slides.title: A TCP web request
body: Identify the application message.
Locate transport, IP and local-link information.
Read the layer order from sender to receiver.
slides.notes: For this explicit TCP example: application data is carried by TCP, IP and a local frame. This is a conceptual layering trace, not a Cisco topology drawing. Pause for predictions before discussing the expected result. Teaching reference: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#networks. Technical/course references: https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc1122 https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc1918 https://senior-secondary.scsa.wa.edu.au/__data/assets/pdf_file/0003/1090875/Year-11_12_Computer-Science_ATAR_Additional-syllabus-support-booklet-.PDF

slides.title: Layer explanations
body: Match routing, a web request and a local frame.
Explain the responsibility behind each match.
slides.notes: Routing belongs to Internet, web messaging to Application, local frames to Network access. Ask for the responsibility rather than memorised position alone. Swap explaining and checking roles so both learners articulate the reasoning. Teaching reference: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#networks. Technical/course references: https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc1122 https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc1918 https://senior-secondary.scsa.wa.edu.au/__data/assets/pdf_file/0003/1090875/Year-11_12_Computer-Science_ATAR_Additional-syllabus-support-booklet-.PDF

slides.title: Independent practice
body: Make a four-layer table from memory.
Add one job and example per layer.
Compare with the chapter, then correct one gap.
slides.notes: Use retrieval, compare, correction and a second closed-book attempt. Keep the model names consistent. Offer the relevant worked example if needed, then use a changed case to check independent understanding. Teaching reference: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#networks. Technical/course references: https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc1122 https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc1918 https://senior-secondary.scsa.wa.edu.au/__data/assets/pdf_file/0003/1090875/Year-11_12_Computer-Science_ATAR_Additional-syllabus-support-booklet-.PDF

slides.title: A choice to explain
body: Which layer handles routing IP packets?
A: Internet
B: Network access
slides.notes: A. The bottom network-access layer handles the local link. Acknowledge that OSI uses different layer names. Give thinking time and collect reasons, without recording scores. Teaching reference: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#networks. Technical/course references: https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc1122 https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc1918 https://senior-secondary.scsa.wa.edu.au/__data/assets/pdf_file/0003/1090875/Year-11_12_Computer-Science_ATAR_Additional-syllabus-support-booklet-.PDF

slides.title: Exit explanation
body: Explain why HTTP alone cannot deliver a page.
Name the other layer responsibilities.
slides.notes: Look for service, transport, routing and local-link roles rather than a list without explanations. Use the response to select the next explanation or practice activity. Teaching reference: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#networks. Technical/course references: https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc1122 https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc1918 https://senior-secondary.scsa.wa.edu.au/__data/assets/pdf_file/0003/1090875/Year-11_12_Computer-Science_ATAR_Additional-syllabus-support-booklet-.PDF

lessons.title: A web request and transport choices
lessons.prepare: Open the networks chapter and its learning resources. Use paper or a local editor as appropriate, with fictional data and disposable practice copies. The suggested 55-minute lesson is flexible.

slides.title: A web request and transport choices
body: Unit 1 · Week 11 · Lesson 3
Trace a request and explain TCP and UDP guarantees.
slides.notes: Explain the goal and the expected independent outcome. Trace a request and explain TCP and UDP guarantees. This is ungraded textbook learning. Suggested times can be adjusted to the class. Teaching reference: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#networks. Technical/course references: https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc1122 https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc1918 https://senior-secondary.scsa.wa.edu.au/__data/assets/pdf_file/0003/1090875/Year-11_12_Computer-Science_ATAR_Additional-syllabus-support-booklet-.PDF

slides.title: Retrieval and explanation
body: Which layer handles IP routing?
What does DNS help a client look up?
slides.notes: Internet handles IP addressing/routing. DNS supplies name-related records, often including an address. It does not carry the later web page content. Allow silent thinking before discussion. Ask a learner to justify an answer before revealing the explanation. Teaching reference: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#networks. Technical/course references: https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc1122 https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc1918 https://senior-secondary.scsa.wa.edu.au/__data/assets/pdf_file/0003/1090875/Year-11_12_Computer-Science_ATAR_Additional-syllabus-support-booklet-.PDF

slides.title: Service and transport roles
table: Does not serve the web page
slides.notes: Choose a web request using TCP for the worked trace. Modern HTTP versions can use other transport arrangements, so do not state all HTTPS uses TCP. Teaching reference: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#networks. Technical/course references: https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc1122 https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc1918 https://senior-secondary.scsa.wa.edu.au/__data/assets/pdf_file/0003/1090875/Year-11_12_Computer-Science_ATAR_Additional-syllabus-support-booklet-.PDF

slides.title: Encapsulation in this example
body: Application data enters a TCP segment.
IP carries that segment in a packet.
A local frame carries the packet across a link.
slides.notes: Explain encapsulation as adding control information for each job. The receiver processes the information up the stack. Pause for predictions before discussing the expected result. Teaching reference: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#networks. Technical/course references: https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc1122 https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc1918 https://senior-secondary.scsa.wa.edu.au/__data/assets/pdf_file/0003/1090875/Year-11_12_Computer-Science_ATAR_Additional-syllabus-support-booklet-.PDF

slides.title: A transport decision
body: A transfer needs an ordered stream.
Another app handles late or missing updates itself.
Discuss the transport responsibilities in each case.
slides.notes: TCP supplies ordered reliable stream behaviour. UDP leaves delivery/order handling to the application where needed. Avoid claiming UDP always wins on speed. Swap explaining and checking roles so both learners articulate the reasoning. Teaching reference: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#networks. Technical/course references: https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc1122 https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc1918 https://senior-secondary.scsa.wa.edu.au/__data/assets/pdf_file/0003/1090875/Year-11_12_Computer-Science_ATAR_Additional-syllabus-support-booklet-.PDF

slides.title: Independent practice
body: Trace a fictional library request through four layers.
Explain where DNS and TLS contribute.
State one guarantee and one limit of TCP.
slides.notes: Learners annotate a paper trace. Do not generate live traffic. Require an explicit assumption that this example uses TCP. Offer the relevant worked example if needed, then use a changed case to check independent understanding. Teaching reference: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#networks. Technical/course references: https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc1122 https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc1918 https://senior-secondary.scsa.wa.edu.au/__data/assets/pdf_file/0003/1090875/Year-11_12_Computer-Science_ATAR_Additional-syllabus-support-booklet-.PDF

slides.title: A choice to explain
body: A TCP connection exists.
A: The application must always be available.
B: The application can still fail or reject a request.
slides.notes: B. Transport guarantees concern the stream, not the whole service or its application permissions. Give thinking time and collect reasons, without recording scores. Teaching reference: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#networks. Technical/course references: https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc1122 https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc1918 https://senior-secondary.scsa.wa.edu.au/__data/assets/pdf_file/0003/1090875/Year-11_12_Computer-Science_ATAR_Additional-syllabus-support-booklet-.PDF

slides.title: Exit explanation
body: Explain segment, packet and frame.
Give one reason a web request can still fail.
slides.notes: Each term identifies a layer unit. DNS, application state or permissions can fail independently of a healthy local connection. Use the response to select the next explanation or practice activity. Teaching reference: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#networks. Technical/course references: https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc1122 https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc1918 https://senior-secondary.scsa.wa.edu.au/__data/assets/pdf_file/0003/1090875/Year-11_12_Computer-Science_ATAR_Additional-syllabus-support-booklet-.PDF

lessons.title: Network evidence and diagnosis
lessons.prepare: Open the networks chapter and its learning resources. Use paper or a local editor as appropriate, with fictional data and disposable practice copies. The suggested 55-minute lesson is flexible.

slides.title: Network evidence and diagnosis
body: Unit 1 · Week 11 · Lesson 4
Use test results to choose a sensible next check.
slides.notes: Explain the goal and the expected independent outcome. Use test results to choose a sensible next check. This is ungraded textbook learning. Suggested times can be adjusted to the class. Teaching reference: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#networks. Technical/course references: https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc1122 https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc1918 https://senior-secondary.scsa.wa.edu.au/__data/assets/pdf_file/0003/1090875/Year-11_12_Computer-Science_ATAR_Additional-syllabus-support-booklet-.PDF

slides.title: Retrieval and explanation
body: Does one successful ping prove a website works?
What part of communication does DNS support?
slides.notes: Ping tests ICMP echo behaviour at a moment. It does not test web-page service or prove all application functions work. Allow silent thinking before discussion. Ask a learner to justify an answer before revealing the explanation. Teaching reference: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#networks. Technical/course references: https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc1122 https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc1918 https://senior-secondary.scsa.wa.edu.au/__data/assets/pdf_file/0003/1090875/Year-11_12_Computer-Science_ATAR_Additional-syllabus-support-booklet-.PDF

slides.title: Observation and next check
slides.notes: The table proposes investigations, not confirmed diagnoses. A device or policy may ignore ICMP while other traffic still works. Teaching reference: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#networks. Technical/course references: https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc1122 https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc1918 https://senior-secondary.scsa.wa.edu.au/__data/assets/pdf_file/0003/1090875/Year-11_12_Computer-Science_ATAR_Additional-syllabus-support-booklet-.PDF

slides.title: A name-resolution clue
body: The name lookup fails.
The known server address replies to ICMP.
Separate the two observations before proposing a cause.
slides.notes: Investigate DNS first. An ICMP reply supports reachability for that test but does not show HTTPS is functional. Do not bypass certificate checks by substituting an IP. Pause for predictions before discussing the expected result. Teaching reference: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#networks. Technical/course references: https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc1122 https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc1918 https://senior-secondary.scsa.wa.edu.au/__data/assets/pdf_file/0003/1090875/Year-11_12_Computer-Science_ATAR_Additional-syllabus-support-booklet-.PDF

slides.title: Evidence pairs
body: Write an observation for a slow service.
Suggest two possible causes.
Name a check that distinguishes them.
slides.notes: Accept congestion versus an overloaded service if the proposed observations separate client/link load from service behaviour. Swap explaining and checking roles so both learners articulate the reasoning. Teaching reference: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#networks. Technical/course references: https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc1122 https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc1918 https://senior-secondary.scsa.wa.edu.au/__data/assets/pdf_file/0003/1090875/Year-11_12_Computer-Science_ATAR_Additional-syllabus-support-booklet-.PDF

slides.title: Independent practice
body: Explain two supplied failure scenarios.
State what is known and what remains uncertain.
Choose the next check and justify it.
slides.notes: Use paper scenarios only. Partners challenge any unsupported certainty, then learners write their own final reasoning. Offer the relevant worked example if needed, then use a changed case to check independent understanding. Teaching reference: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#networks. Technical/course references: https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc1122 https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc1918 https://senior-secondary.scsa.wa.edu.au/__data/assets/pdf_file/0003/1090875/Year-11_12_Computer-Science_ATAR_Additional-syllabus-support-booklet-.PDF

slides.title: A choice to explain
body: A client receives no ping reply.
A: The server is certainly switched off.
B: Link, routing, policy or host causes remain possible.
slides.notes: B. A failed test narrows the question only when its assumptions and limits are considered. Give thinking time and collect reasons, without recording scores. Teaching reference: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#networks. Technical/course references: https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc1122 https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc1918 https://senior-secondary.scsa.wa.edu.au/__data/assets/pdf_file/0003/1090875/Year-11_12_Computer-Science_ATAR_Additional-syllabus-support-booklet-.PDF

slides.title: Exit explanation
body: Correct the claim “ping works, so the website works”.
Give one useful follow-up check.
slides.notes: Expected: ICMP and application service are different. A relevant follow-up checks name resolution, service response or access configuration. Use the response to select the next explanation or practice activity. Teaching reference: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#networks. Technical/course references: https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc1122 https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc1918 https://senior-secondary.scsa.wa.edu.au/__data/assets/pdf_file/0003/1090875/Year-11_12_Computer-Science_ATAR_Additional-syllabus-support-booklet-.PDF
